chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning

A man performed li‘an with his wife while she was pregnant, then after she gave birth he claimed her child and asserted that he was from him. He said: “The child is returned to him, and he is not flogged, because the mutual imprecation has already passed.”

key_terms.لَاعَنَ: he performed li‘an, the formal mutual imprecation between spouses
key_terms.يُرَدُّ إِلَيْهِ: is returned or attributed back to him
key_terms.ٱدَّعَى: he claimed or asserted legal attribution
key_terms.ٱلتَّلَاعُنُ: the process of mutual imprecation having occurred

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man claims a child after performing li‘an with his pregnant wife?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man who had entered into li‘an with his pregnant wife and later claimed the child after birth. The Imam عليه السلام states that the child is attributed back to him, while no hadd punishment is applied to him because the process of mutual imprecation had already taken place.
